Negative progression kills this game. In normal, well designed games, the more you play, the stronger you get. But in this game, like in so many other disappointing roguelikes, the more you play, the weaker you get. Not because the game gets harder, no. Because the pool of items and options get diluted, more and more and more. Until you reach a point where winning is no longer a matter of choices but of luck. This game feels great. It has a fun loop, it looks good and feels nice to play. And I can see potential builds that could be strong and fun when looking at the list of items. There is a good game hiding there, but it won't show up until the devs fix that problem.

It's fine. It's fun to begin with but once you begin to unlock new items, which by at least most rationale should be a net positive, the fun turns to frustration. It becomes: Check first two islands for any potential synergistic items. Find none. Find 140 holy shields and feathers. Reset. Repeat around 20 times and final get some sort of synergy. Get to hydra. Die. Try another 30 times. Finally find a synergy that works. Win. Maybe 1 in 5000 holy shields is a win. See over 10,000 holy shields before your next win. Banish holy shield. It's spot is now filled with one of the 40 other garbage items in the game. Probably rusty ring. Find nearly 432 rusty rings. You have 4 banishes, so you can get rid of roughly 1% of the holy shields and rusty rings. Don't worry though because you're about to uncover over 600 royal horns. Start a band. Win. Honestly, the banishes feel like trying to stop a river from running by slapping some flex seal on a rock and praying the dulcet tones of your royal horn will reverberate just right off the acoustic shell you've built out of the 10,000 holy shields you've found to land yourself a record deal so you can afford to stop adventuring. Build a house out of holy shields and fill it with a library of books that are only useful once. Live happily ever after....holy shield.

I’ve got three main issues with this game, which is RNG, boss gimmicks and the unlock system being terrible. RNG: the gear itself in this game is bound to be RNG based, but there should be some way to not be entirely reliant on getting good encounters once you hit the 3rd difficulty. Bosses: the gimmicks either ♥♥♥♥ your build up or don't. For example: there's a boss that completely ignores your armor and a boss that just deletes it, so if you use armor as defense, then ur ♥♥♥♥♥♥ even the final boss in the forest just forces you to just build into high dmg, because it gets 1 extra dmg every turn, which wouldn't be bad if forest loot didn't mostly give u synergies for stall builds (and some bosses actively punishing glass cannons) Unlocks: the unlock system feels terrible for a game this short because it's just random tasks like "get 50 str", "defeat the second boss before the first cycle is over", "lick the left part of woodland abominations nutsack for 2.3 seconds" for a game that is replayable. It wouldn't be that bad, but this game isn't that replayable (except for kingmaker its actually decently replayable) Side note: I put some hours into kingmaker and the other players are either dumb as ♥♥♥♥ or have the most insane build ever.

While I did have fun at first, the game runs out of engaging content way too quickly. You'll beat the first map in an hour or two, then go the second map. Once you beat those two, you look at the game and say, "That was great! What's next?" You'll see the sweat rolling down it's face as you wait for a reply because that's it, you've seen just about all it has to offer. "Well you can grind for hours to achieve many luck-dependent items," the game will tell you. Most of the unlock conditions are hidden from you, and so many others require multiple specific items. You waste so much time restarting over and over trying to get the exact item combos required. It's straight up not fun to unlock items in this game, but that's all there is to do since the gameplay itself is so basic. "Take a break from the endless item grind with PvP!" the game will offer. No thanks. Sure there is PvP, but it's like saying you can go PvP someone at the roulette table. You can make most vague of plans, but actually no control over anything. In singleplayer, bosses are designed with strengths and weakness. PvP strips this consistency out, leaving you to just aimlessly walk around a map to see who can RNG better items. It's devoid of any strategy and only further highlights the underlying problems with the game. This game has been in Early Access for almost a year, yet of the 13 patches, only one added any real content to PvE. The others are bug fixes but the rest are just wasted on PvP balance changes. Why do entire updates need to be buffing / nerfing item stats, adding truly nothing to the game. At this point, I honestly doubt if the game will even get the third map, since they removed reference of it in-game. The game isn't hopeless. I'm sure the devs care and content can be added. Item unlocks are painful, but really it's just due to having such a limited inventory, combined with having already seen all the game's content. Probably worth $5, maybe $10 if you really got nothing better to buy. It needs the third map, and honestly a forth as well, to be even close to worth the $20 asking price.

Lucky for me, He is Coming manages to fix whatever my brain felt was "wrong" with Loop Hero. If I had to put my finger on it, it's just the more direct player agency regarding where you move and what you pick and the way uncovering new map knowledge informs your decision making at every step. The player agency impact on the build feels direct and immediate instead of indirect and delayed while keeping all the good aspects of Loop Hero. And the two sync and async multiplayer modes are just super smartly implemented and the chef's kiss.

Amazing game that absolutely hooks you. It takes the loot/gear build synergy of Diablo 2 and presents it in a mid 80s Ultima style flavour. The result is completely awesome. The reliance on RNG that some people are complaining about is laughable - the loops are so quick and painless that you just get up and jump right back in. If you get demolished by the first boss who cares? Roguelikes with permadeath are not supposed to be faceroll power fantasies; they do not give a crap about your feelings and sensitivities. Start over and smash him next time. I played the latest content "The Gauntlet", for maybe 3 hours and got one single victory alongside dozens of deaths. I had a blast the entire time.

I really enjoy the core game loop, but it feels like a crapshoot in just hoping for one of the 3 or 4 combinations that can beat the boss I'm facing that day. I can't recommend this game because it feels like you're just at the whims of the RNG, often realizing a run is dead in the first day because I haven't been able to find anything that synergizes. In most other roguelikes you have multiple ways of manipulating your luck to get items you need-- shop rerolls, rerolls, banishing items, and themed areas are all pretty common. He is Coming [i]does[/i] have that sort of luck manipulation, but barely so. You unlock more as you complete the compendium, however, you also get vastly more junk that you need to filter through, ironically making it harder to get the items you need / want. There are ways of transmuting items into other random items, but.. frankly why would I want to use this? The only time I would ever care is if I have an inventory full of garbage, but often times transmuting items just gives me something worse since it can't even guarantee me an item of the same type. Also, please rework the Gauntlet mode. I feel like it's only balanced through sheer merit of everyone getting equivalent garbage. The progression in the multiplayer is essentially "pick one of up to 4 paths", repeat two or three times per floor, then face another player. However, the fundamental problem is that you could get 2 paths of 4 monsters (which only give a bit of gold), start the game with a "Transmute an item!" node (while having no items aside from your starting weapon), etc. Basically, you have to hope and pray you'll get relevant items because there's no weighted RNG or guardrails in place to ensure you get the bare minimum to have fun. But genuinely, aside from the mechanical issues this is a fantastically designed games. The artstyle is fun and goofy, the music is fantastic, the core gameplay loop [i]could[/i] be addictive if they only smoothed out some of the edges. Hoping that this game improves in the future, and also eventually releases on mobile, since I know it could be the type of thing I dump hundreds of hours into.

I really like this game. There is no too much thinking in a run, you start with something, you pick up items to make a strong set and run with it. Don't need to overthink it. The runs are short, maybe a full kingmaker run takes about 30 minutes. I really like the autobattle feature of this game. No need to waste time on battles and planning before a run which became very boring to me after a while in Darkest Dungeon. Some says singleplayer mode is short because the 2 available map (which will be 3 in the future) can be beaten in 2-5 hours. However unlocking all the items took me about 15 hours. Kingmaker mode is where you face other players as bosses, I had plenty of fun with that too. Absolutely worth the price.
